Elevating an agent from a thinker to an executor slashes token costs, reduces latency, and eliminates the recurrence of past errors. Even with a structured architecture, an AI that retains every synthesized insight will eventually choke on its own accumulated data. This leads to slow corruption, a mathematical certainty that stale, outdated state information will actively derail current tasks if left untouched in the database. This is an effing house forgetting curve. For an artificial agent, this decay is a requirement. Low-V value memories must systematically weaken and drop out over time. Managing the memory life cycle involves a disciplined six-step policy. Acquire, encode, derive, retrieve, use, and finally forgetting. Attempting to bake facts directly into the mathematical weights of the neural network avoids this policy, but risks catastrophic forgetting where new information inadvertently overwrites critical existing capabilities. Persistent intelligence relies on the architectural discipline to route data, compile skills, and prune the noise that no longer matters.
